profile.address: 13275, Minuteman Drive, Draper Old Farm, Draper, Salt Lake County, Utah, 84020
profile.reading:
FiberState operates a data center it refers to internally as SLC1, serving the Salt Lake City, Utah market from a location in Draper, in Salt Lake County. The company's own site lists 106 East 13200 South in Draper as its main office address, while the coordinates recorded for this registry entry resolve to a separate nearby address on Minuteman Drive in Draper's Old Farm neighborhood. Both are Draper addresses within a few miles of each other, and FiberState's materials do not explicitly state whether its office and its data center floor are the same building, so the exact street address of the technical space itself is treated here as unconfirmed rather than settled.

Draper sits at the southern end of the Salt Lake Valley and is part of the corridor sometimes called Silicon Slopes, which has drawn a growing number of technology companies and data center operators over the past decade because of relatively low power costs, a dry climate favorable to free air cooling, and proximity to fiber routes running along the Wasatch Front. FiberState positions itself in that market as a provider of dedicated bare metal servers, colocation, IP transit, disaster recovery, and hosting infrastructure, with recent additions aimed at customers running artificial intelligence and machine learning workloads.

On the technical side, FiberState advertises a carrier neutral facility with six Tier 1 network providers connecting on site, including Lumen Technologies, Zayo, Cogent Communications, Hurricane Electric, and GTT, with port speeds up to 400 gigabits and what the company calls modular, dynamic expansion capacity. The company states its network redundancy is built on an N plus one model and backs its service with a 99.9 percent uptime guarantee, with distributed denial of service protection included by default rather than sold as an add on.

FiberState does not publish a square footage figure for the SLC1 facility, a power capacity in kilowatts or megawatts, a construction or opening date, or details of its backup generation and cooling systems, and no independent county property or permit record for the facility was reachable to fill those gaps. Those figures are recorded here as unpublished. What is public is a services and connectivity profile aimed at small and mid sized businesses and at newer AI focused customers looking for a Utah based alternative to larger national colocation providers.

reading.body:
FiberState publishes no power capacity or square footage for its Salt Lake City data center. The operator's website describes the facility as offering colocation, dedicated servers, peering, and IP transit services with named carrier and exchange partners, but does not state the data center's physical location or size. No compute density or IT load can be estimated from published data.

Utah has 21 mapped data center facilities, of which 9 publish power capacity totaling 52.18 MW. FiberState's ranking at position 10 by published megawatts reflects the fact that it publishes no specification at all, placing it below the nine facilities with disclosed capacity. The state's published capacity is thin, and most mapped facilities here disclose no figures.

Without published power, footprint, or utilization data, this facility cannot be assessed for relevance to AI infrastructure scaling. The operator should publish its capacity to enable evaluation.
